stem: Ahmed is 7 years old and has exercise-induced asthma. He only gets symptoms when playing at school or playing soccer at the weekend. Which is the best single method to prevent exercise-induced asthma symptoms?

options.text: Cover the nose and mouth initially whilst playing to reduce cold air inhalation

explanation: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction is commonly prevented with a short-acting beta2-agonist such as salbutamol taken shortly before exercise. Warm-up strategies and avoiding cold air may help some patients, and montelukast can be used in selected cases, but pre-exercise salbutamol is the standard first-line single best answer.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: This item was rewritten from a multiple-answer format into a single-best-answer question because more than one option could be considered helpful. Pre-exercise salbutamol is the clearest best answer.

optionExplanations.A: May reduce symptoms in some children, but it is not the most effective single preventive measure.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. A short-acting beta2-agonist taken before exercise is first-line prevention for exercise-induced asthma.
optionExplanations.C: May help by reducing cold-air exposure, but it is supportive rather than the best single preventive treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Can be used as controller therapy in some patients, but it is not the usual first-line immediate prevention for exercise symptoms.
